en: Boiling liquid water for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria, making it safe to drink.
Mixing liquid bleach with acidic vinegar creates toxic chlorine gas, which is dangerous to breathe.
Bacteria cause chemical changes in milk, producing sour acids that make the spoiled liquid unsafe to drink.
Rubbing alcohol is highly flammable, so you must keep liquid bottles away from open flames or hot stoves.
Dissolving solid oral rehydration salts in clean water creates a solution that treats childhood dehydration.
Heating a sealed aerosol gas can increases internal pressure, which can cause the metal container to explode.
Peanut proteins remain in baked mixtures even after heating, causing severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.
Liquid water instantly turns into expanding steam when dropped into hot cooking oil, causing dangerous splatters.
Foam life jackets float because their solid material is less dense than liquid water, keeping swimmers safe.
Your stomach produces hydrochloric acid, a corrosive liquid that chemically breaks down solid food for digestion.
Liquid water expands when it freezes into solid ice, which can burst closed metal pipes during cold nights.
N95 masks filter solid dust particles from the air we breathe, protecting our lungs from pollution.
